finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get. An attacker can make the server request any URL, including internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) and localhost. The response body is copied back to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response streamed back via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: The /fetch route is registered to the fetch handler with no authentication or middleware.
The attacker-controlled `target` is read from the query string.
`target` goes to http.Get with no validation. The default client follows redirects and allows http and https to any host or IP.
The upstream response body is written to the attacker, which exposes the contents.

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, host allowlist, IP or private-range blocklist, DNS-rebinding protection, redirect restriction or authentication on this path. The `allowed` map at main.go:9 is used only by safeFetch, not by fetch.

verdict.reason: main.go:15 reads the query param `target` and main.go:16 passes it unvalidated to http.Get, with the body returned at main.go:22. The route at main.go:41 has no middleware, and the allowlist at main.go:27 is only in safeFetch.
